title.zh: 卷一百一十七 載記第十七 姚興上
title.en: Volume 117 Records 17: Yao Xing Part One
title.raw: 卷一百一十七 載記第十七 姚興上 Volume 117 Records 17: Yao Xing Part One

sentences.zh: 姚興

translations.literal: Yao Xing
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing

translations.literal: (Part One)
translations.idiomatic: (Part One)

sentences.zh: 姚興，字子略，萇之長子也。

translations.literal: Yao Xing, styled Zilüe, was the eldest son of Yao Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing, whose courtesy name was Zilüe, was the eldest son of Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 苻堅時為太子舍人。

translations.literal: Under Fu Jian he served as Gentleman Attendant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: During Fu Jian's reign he held the office of Gentleman Attendant to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 萇之在馬牧，興自長安冒難奔萇，萇立為皇太子。

translations.literal: When Chang was at the Horse Pastures, Xing braved danger from Chang'an to flee to Chang, and Chang established him as imperial heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: While Yao Chang was stationed at the Horse Pastures, Yao Xing braved peril to flee from Chang'an and join him, and Yao Chang installed him as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 萇出征討，常留統後事。

translations.literal: Whenever Chang went out on campaign, he always left Xing behind to oversee rear affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yao Chang marched on campaign, he routinely left Yao Xing behind to manage affairs in the rear.

sentences.zh: 及鎮長安，甚有威惠。

translations.literal: When he garrisoned Chang'an, he was greatly awe-inspiring and beneficent.
translations.idiomatic: When he held Chang'an, he ruled with both stern authority and kindness.

sentences.zh: 與其中舍人梁喜、洗馬範勖等講論經籍，不以兵難廢業，時人咸化之。

translations.literal: With Palace Gentleman Liang Xi, Groom Fan Xu, and others he discussed the classics; he did not abandon study because of military troubles; people of the time were all transformed by him.
translations.idiomatic: He debated the classics with Liang Xi, Gentleman of the Palace Within, Fan Xu, Groom of the Heir Apparent, and others, refusing to abandon scholarship because of the hardships of war; his contemporaries took inspiration from him.

sentences.zh: 萇死，興秘不發喪，以其叔父緒鎮安定，碩德鎮陰密，弟崇守長安。

translations.literal: When Chang died, Xing kept it secret and did not announce mourning; he had his uncle Xu garrison Anding, Shuode garrison Yinmi, and younger brother Chong defend Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chang died, Yao Xing concealed the death and withheld the obsequies; he assigned his uncle Yao Xu to hold Anding, Yao Shuode to hold Yinmi, and his younger brother Yao Chong to defend Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 碩德將佐言於碩德曰：「公威名宿重，部曲最強，今喪代之際，朝廷必相猜忌，非永安之道也。

translations.literal: Shuode's generals and aides said to Shuode: "Your lordship's fearsome name is long established and your personal troops are the strongest; now at the juncture of succession the court is sure to turn suspicious; this is no way to lasting security.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shuode's subordinates said to him: "Your prestige has stood for years and your command is the strongest force at hand; at a moment of imperial succession the court will inevitably grow wary of you; that is no path to lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 宜奔秦州，觀望事勢。

translations.literal: You ought to flee to Qinzhou and watch how circumstances develop.
translations.idiomatic: You should withdraw to Qinzhou and see how the situation unfolds.

sentences.zh: 」碩德曰：「太子志度寬明，必無疑阻。

translations.literal: " Shuode said: "The heir apparent's mind is generous and clear; there will surely be no suspicion or obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shuode replied: "The crown prince is broad-minded and discerning; he will not harbor groundless doubts or block our way.

sentences.zh: 今苻登未滅而自尋干戈，所謂追二袁之蹤，授首與人。

translations.literal: Now Fu Deng is not yet destroyed yet we would seek strife among ourselves—what is called following in the footsteps of the two Yuans and handing our heads to another.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng still lives; if we now turn our blades on one another, we shall only repeat the folly of the two Yuans and hand victory to someone else.

sentences.zh: 吾死而已，終不若斯。

translations.literal: I would rather die; I will never be like that.
translations.idiomatic: I would sooner die than follow such counsel.

sentences.zh: 」及至，興優禮而遣之。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Xing treated him with exceptional courtesy and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Shuode arrived, Yao Xing received him with exceptional courtesy and let him return to his post.

sentences.zh: 興自稱大將軍，以尹緯為長史，狄伯支為司馬，率眾伐苻登。

translations.literal: Xing styled himself Grand General; he appointed Yin Wei as Chief Clerk and Di Bozhi as Marshal, and led the host to attack Fu Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing took the title of Grand General, appointed Yin Wei as Chief Clerk and Di Bozhi as Marshal, and led the army against Fu Deng.

sentences.zh: 咸陽太守劉忌奴據避世堡以叛，興襲忌奴，擒之。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Xianyang Liu Jinu occupied Bishibao and rebelled; Xing attacked Jinu and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jinu, Administrator of Xianyang, seized Bishibao and rose in rebellion; Yao Xing struck him, took him prisoner, and subdued the revolt.

sentences.zh: 苻登自六陌向廢橋，始平太守姚詳據馬嵬堡以距登。

translations.literal: Fu Deng advanced from Liumo toward Feiqiao; the Administrator of Shiping Yao Xiang held Maweibao to resist Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng marched from Liumo toward Feiqiao; Yao Xiang, Administrator of Shiping, entrenched himself at Maweibao to hold Fu Deng at bay.

sentences.zh: 登眾甚盛，興慮詳不能遏，乃自將精騎以迫登，遣尹緯領步卒赴詳。

translations.literal: Deng's forces were very strong; Xing worried Xiang could not stop them, so he personally led picked cavalry to press Deng and sent Yin Wei to lead infantry to reinforce Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng's army was formidable; Yao Xing feared Yao Xiang could not contain it, so he personally led elite horsemen to pressure Fu Deng while dispatching Yin Wei with foot soldiers to reinforce Yao Xiang.

sentences.zh: 緯用詳計，據廢橋以抗登。

translations.literal: Wei adopted Xiang's plan and held Feiqiao to resist Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Wei followed Yao Xiang's plan and secured Feiqiao to block Fu Deng.

sentences.zh: 登因急攻緯，緯將出戰，興馳遣狄伯支謂緯曰：「兵法不戰而制人者，蓋為此也。

translations.literal: Deng therefore pressed the attack on Wei; Wei was about to go out to fight when Xing urgently sent Di Bozhi to tell Wei: "The art of war's 'subdue others without fighting'—this is surely what it means.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng redoubled his assault on Yin Wei; as Yin Wei was about to give battle, Yao Xing urgently sent Di Bozhi with orders: "The maxim that the adept warrior wins without fighting is meant for moments such as this.

sentences.zh: 苻登窮寇，宜持重，不可輕戰。

translations.literal: Fu Deng is a cornered bandit; you should hold firm and must not fight lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng is a desperate foe; stand firm and do not hazard a rash engagement.

sentences.zh: 」緯曰：「先帝登遐，人情擾懼，今不因思奮之力，梟殄逆豎，大事去矣。

translations.literal: " Wei said: "The late emperor has ascended on high; men's hearts are disturbed and afraid; if we do not now rely on the power of those who yearn to strive and behead and exterminate the rebellious villain, the great enterprise is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Wei answered: "The late sovereign has just passed away; fear and uncertainty grip the army. If we do not seize this surge of loyal resolve to strike down the traitor Fu Deng, the whole enterprise is lost.

sentences.zh: 緯敢以死爭。

translations.literal: Wei dares to contend with death.
translations.idiomatic: I am prepared to stake my life on this battle.

sentences.zh: 」遂與登戰，大破之，登眾渴死者十二三，其夜大潰，登奔雍。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he fought Deng and utterly defeated him; two or three men in ten of Deng's army died of thirst; that night they broke in great disorder; Deng fled to Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He engaged Fu Deng and won a crushing victory; two or three men in ten of Fu Deng's army perished of thirst, and that night the enemy ranks collapsed in panic as Fu Deng fled toward Yong.

sentences.zh: 興乃發喪行服。

translations.literal: Xing then announced the mourning and observed mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Yao Xing publicly announce his father's death and don mourning garb.

sentences.zh: 太元十九年，僭即帝位於槐里，大赦境內，改元曰皇初，遂如安定。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Taiyuan, he usurped the imperial title at Huaili, issued a general amnesty within the realm, changed the era name to Huangchu, and then went to Anding.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of the Jin Taiyuan era he presumptuously assumed the throne at Huaili, proclaimed a general amnesty throughout his realm, adopted the reign title Huangchu, and then proceeded to Anding.

sentences.zh: 先是，苻登使弟廣守雍，子崇屯胡空堡，聞登敗，各棄守走。

translations.literal: Earlier, Fu Deng had sent younger brother Guang to defend Yong and son Chong to encamp at Hukongbao; hearing of Deng's defeat, each abandoned his post and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Fu Deng had stationed his brother Fu Guang at Yong and his son Fu Chong at Hukongbao; when they heard of his defeat, both abandoned their positions and fled.

sentences.zh: 登無所投據，遂奔平涼，率其餘眾入馬毛山。

translations.literal: Deng had nowhere to turn; he fled to Pingliang and led his remaining host into Maomaoshan.
translations.idiomatic: With no refuge left, Fu Deng rushed to Pingliang and led his surviving troops into the Maomao Hills.

sentences.zh: 興自安定如涇陽，與登戰于山南，斬登。

translations.literal: Xing went from Anding to Jingyang and fought Deng south of the mountain; he beheaded Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing marched from Anding to Jingyang, fought Fu Deng south of the mountains, and slew him in the field.

sentences.zh: 散其部眾，歸復農業。

translations.literal: He dispersed Deng's troops and returned them to farming.
translations.idiomatic: He disbanded Fu Deng's soldiers and sent them back to their fields.

sentences.zh: 徙陰密三萬戶于長安，分大營戶為四，置四軍以領之。

translations.literal: He moved thirty thousand households from Yinmi to Chang'an, divided the great camp households into four, and established four armies to command them.
translations.idiomatic: He relocated thirty thousand households from Yinmi to Chang'an, split the former great camp population into four divisions, and created four armies to command them.

sentences.zh: 安南強熙、鎮遠楊多叛，推竇沖為盟主，所在擾亂。

translations.literal: Qiang Xi the Pacifier of the South and Yang Duo the Stabilizer of the Distance rebelled; they set up Dou Chong as covenant lord; everywhere was disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Xi, General Who Pacifies the South, and Yang Duo, General Who Stabilizes the Distance, rose in revolt and proclaimed Dou Chong their leader; unrest spread across the region.

sentences.zh: 興率諸將討之，軍次武功，多兄子良國殺多而降。

translations.literal: Xing led the generals to punish them; the army halted at Wugong; Yang Duo's nephew Liangguo killed Duo and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing led his commanders against them and camped at Wugong, where Yang Liangguo, Yang Duo's nephew, assassinated Yang Duo and came over to Yao Xing's side.

sentences.zh: 沖弟彰武與沖離貳，沖奔強熙。

translations.literal: Chong's younger brother Zhangwu fell out with Chong; Chong fled to Qiang Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chong's younger brother Dou Zhangwu broke with him, so Dou Chong fled to join Qiang Xi.

sentences.zh: 熙聞興將至，率戶二千奔秦州。

translations.literal: Xi heard Xing was coming and led two thousand households to flee to Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiang Xi learned that Yao Xing was approaching, he took two thousand households and fled toward Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 竇沖走汧川，汧川氐仇高執送之。

translations.literal: Dou Chong fled to Qianchuan; the Di of Qianchuan Qiu Gao seized him and sent him in.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chong fled to Qianchuan, where Qiu Gao of the local Di people seized him and delivered him to the court.

sentences.zh: 沖從弟統率其眾降於興。

translations.literal: Chong's cousin Tong led his host to surrender to Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chong's cousin Dou Tong led the remainder of the rebel forces to surrender to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 封征虜緒為晉王，征西碩德為隴西王，征南靖等及功臣尹緯、齊難、楊佛嵩等並為公侯，其餘封爵各有差。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed Xu the Subduer of Captives as Prince of Jin, Shuode the West Campaigner as Prince of Longxi, Jing the South Campaigner and others and meritorious subjects Yin Wei, Qi Nan, Yang Fosong, and others as dukes and marquises; the rest received enfeoffments of varying rank.
translations.idiomatic: He invested Yao Xu, General Who Subdues Invaders, as Prince of Jin; Yao Shuode, General Who Campaigns West, as Prince of Longxi; Yao Jing, General Who Campaigns South, together with such merit holders as Yin Wei, Qi Nan, and Yang Fosong, received ducal or marquisal rank; other officers were ennobled according to their deeds.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑薛勃於貳城為魏軍所伐，遣使請救，使姚崇赴救。

translations.literal: The Xianbei Xue Bo at Ercheng was attacked by Wei forces; he sent envoys asking for aid; Xing sent Yao Chong to relieve him.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei leader Xue Bo, holding Ercheng, was attacked by Wei troops; he appealed for rescue, and Yao Xing sent Yao Chong to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 魏師既還，薛勃復叛，崇伐而執之，大收其士馬而還。

translations.literal: After the Wei army withdrew, Xue Bo rebelled again; Chong attacked and captured him, greatly collected his soldiers and horses, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wei army withdrew, Xue Bo rebelled again; Yao Chong campaigned against him, took him captive, seized large numbers of men and mounts, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 興追尊其庶母孫氏為皇太后，配饗太廟。

translations.literal: Xing posthumously honored his father's concubine Lady Sun as Empress Dowager and accorded her joint sacrifice in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing posthumously elevated his father's concubine, Lady Sun, to Empress Dowager and granted her a place beside the royal ancestors in the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 楊盛保仇池，遣使請命，拜使持節、鎮南將軍、仇池公。

translations.literal: Yang Sheng held Qiuchi and sent envoys suing for appointment; he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Guards the South, and Duke of Qiuchi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sheng, who held Qiuchi, sent envoys suing for recognition; Yao Xing appointed him Bearer of the Imperial Staff, General Who Guards the South, and Duke of Qiuchi.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑越質詰歸率戶二萬叛乞伏乾歸，降於興，興處之于成紀，拜使持節、鎮西將軍、平襄公。

translations.literal: The Xianbei Yuezhi Jiegui led twenty thousand households to rebel against Qifu Gangui and surrender to Xing; Xing settled them at Chengji and appointed him Bearer of the Staff, General Who Guards the West, and Duke of Pingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei chief Yuezhi Jiegui led twenty thousand households in breaking away from Qifu Gangui and submitting to Yao Xing; Yao Xing resettled them at Chengji and named him Bearer of the Imperial Staff, General Who Guards the West, and Duke of Pingxiang.

sentences.zh: 姚碩德討平涼胡金豹於洛城，克之。

translations.literal: Yao Shuode attacked the Pingliang Hu Jin Bao at Luocheng and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shuode campaigned against the Pingliang Hu leader Jin Bao at Luocheng and captured the town.

sentences.zh: 初，上邽薑乳據本縣以叛，自稱秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jiang Ru of Shanggui held his home county in rebellion and styled himself Inspector of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jiang Ru of Shanggui had seized his home county, rebelled, and declared himself Inspector of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 碩德進討之，乳率眾降。

translations.literal: Shuode advanced to attack him; Ru led his host to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shuode advanced against him; Jiang Ru led his forces in surrender.

sentences.zh: 以碩德為秦州牧，領護東羌校尉，鎮上邽。

translations.literal: He appointed Shuode as Governor of Qinzhou, concurrently Colonel Who Protects the Eastern Qiang, and garrisoned Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: He named Yao Shuode Governor of Qinzhou, with the additional post of Colonel Who Protects the Eastern Qiang, and stationed him at Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 征乳為尚書。

translations.literal: He summoned Ru to serve as Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Jiang Ru to the capital to serve as a Minister of State.

sentences.zh: 強熙及略陽豪族權幹城率眾三萬圍上邽，碩德擊破之。

translations.literal: Qiang Xi and the magnate of Lueyang Quan Gancheng led thirty thousand to besiege Shanggui; Shuode defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Xi and Quan Gancheng, a powerful clan leader from Lueyang, brought thirty thousand men to besiege Shanggui; Yao Shuode broke their army.

sentences.zh: 熙南奔仇池，遂假道歸晉。

translations.literal: Xi fled south to Qiuchi and then borrowed passage to return to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Xi fled south to Qiuchi and from there obtained safe conduct into Eastern Jin territory.

sentences.zh: 碩德西討幹城，幹城降。

translations.literal: Shuode campaigned west against Gancheng; Gancheng surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shuode then marched west against Quan Gancheng, who capitulated.

sentences.zh: 興令郡國各歲貢清行孝廉一人。

translations.literal: Xing ordered each commandery and kingdom annually to recommend one pure-conduct filial and incorrupt candidate.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing decreed that every commandery and princedom should each year nominate one candidate for the Filial and Incorrupt examination who excelled in moral conduct.

sentences.zh: 慕容永既為慕容垂所滅，河東太守柳恭等各阻兵自守，興遣姚緒討之。

translations.literal: After Murong Yong had been destroyed by Murong Chui, the Administrators of Hedong Liu Gong and others each held troops and defended themselves; Xing sent Yao Xu to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: After Murong Chui had destroyed Murong Yong, regional administrators such as Liu Gong of Hedong dug in with their own troops; Yao Xing dispatched Yao Xu to reduce them.

sentences.zh: 恭等依河距守，緒不得濟。

translations.literal: Gong and the others relied on the river to defend; Xu could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gong and his allies held the Yellow River line, and Yao Xu could not force a crossing.

sentences.zh: 鎮東薛強先據楊氏壁，引緒從龍門濟河，遂入蒲阪。

translations.literal: Xue Qiang the East Stabilizer first held Yangshi Stockade and guided Xu from Longmen to cross the river; thereupon they entered Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Qiang, the general holding the east, had already occupied Yangshi Stockade; he guided Yao Xu across the river at Longmen, and the army entered Puban.

sentences.zh: 恭勢屈，請降。

translations.literal: Gong's situation gave way and he asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his position collapse, Liu Gong offered his surrender.

sentences.zh: 徙新平、安定新戶六千于蒲阪。

translations.literal: He moved six thousand new households from Xinping and Anding to Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing resettled six thousand newly registered households from Xinping and Anding in Puban.

sentences.zh: 興母虵氏死，興哀毀過禮，不親庶政。

translations.literal: Xing's mother Lady She died; Xing's grief wasted him beyond the rites and he did not personally attend to routine government.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing's mother, Lady She, died; he mourned so fiercely that he exceeded prescribed ritual and ceased to handle daily affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 群臣議請依漢、魏故事，既葬即吉。

translations.literal: The ministers deliberated and asked to follow Han and Wei precedent—after burial return to auspicious dress at once.
translations.idiomatic: His ministers debated the matter and urged him to follow Han and Wei precedent by ending mourning as soon as the burial was complete.

sentences.zh: 興尚書郎李嵩上疏曰「三王異制，五帝殊禮。

translations.literal: Li Song, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, submitted a memorial saying: "The Three Kings had differing systems; the Five Emperors had diverse rites.
translations.idiomatic: Li Song, a Gentleman at the Masters of Writing, presented a memorial: "The Three Ages knew variant institutions; the Five Emperors observed differing rites.

sentences.zh: 孝治天下，先王之高事也，宜遵聖性，以光道訓。

translations.literal: Filial piety rules the realm—it is the supreme affair of the former kings; one ought to follow sagely nature to brighten the way of instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Governing the world through filial devotion was the highest priority of the ancient sages; Your Majesty should heed your own humane nature and thereby illuminate moral teaching.

sentences.zh: 既葬之後，應素服臨朝，率先天下，仁孝之舉也。

translations.literal: After burial, plain garments should attend court, leading all under Heaven—it is an act of benevolent filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: After the interment you should hold court in plain hemp, setting an example for the realm—such is the conduct of humane filial piety.

sentences.zh: 」尹緯駁曰：「帝王喪制，漢、魏為准。

translations.literal: " Yin Wei refuted: "For imperial mourning regulations, Han and Wei are the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Wei objected: "Imperial mourning law takes the Han and Wei codes as its touchstone.

sentences.zh: 嵩矯常越禮，愆於軌度，請付有司，以專擅論。

translations.literal: Song bends the norm and oversteps ritual; he errs against measure—please hand him to the authorities for judgment on presumption.
translations.idiomatic: Li Song twists convention and oversteps ritual propriety; he departs from proper bounds. Hand him to the judicial officials and try him for overstepping authority.

sentences.zh: 既葬即吉，乞依前議。

translations.literal: After burial return to auspicious dress—we beg to follow the earlier deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: End mourning when the burial is finished; we respectfully ask that you adhere to the ministers' original proposal.

sentences.zh: 」興曰：「嵩忠臣孝子，有何咎乎？

translations.literal: " Xing said: "Song is a loyal minister and filial son—what fault is there?
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing said: "Li Song speaks as a loyal minister and a devoted son. Where lies his offense?

sentences.zh: 尹僕射棄先王之典，而欲遵漢、魏之權制，豈所望於朝賢哉！

translations.literal: Director Yin casts aside the canons of the former kings yet wishes to follow Han and Wei's expedient regulations—is this what is expected of court worthies!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Director Yin Wei would discard the models of the ancient kings and cling to the expedients of Han and Wei—is that what we expect of worthy ministers?

sentences.zh: 其一依嵩議。」

translations.literal: In all matters follow Song's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Let everything be decided according to Li Song's memorial.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑薛勃叛奔嶺北，上郡、貳川雜胡皆應之，遂圍安遠將軍姚詳于金城。

translations.literal: The Xianbei Xue Bo rebelled and fled north of the ranges; the miscellaneous Hu of Shangjun and Erchuan all responded; thereupon they besieged Yao Xiang the General Who Pacifies the Distance at Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei Xue Bo rebelled and fled beyond the northern ranges; mixed Hu peoples of Shang Commandery and the Er River basin rose with him, and together they besieged Yao Xiang, General Who Pacifies the Distance, at Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 遣姚崇、尹緯討之。

translations.literal: He sent Yao Chong and Yin Wei to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing dispatched Yao Chong and Yin Wei to suppress the revolt.

sentences.zh: 勃自三交趣金城，崇列營掎之，而租運不繼，三軍大饑。

translations.literal: Bo hurried from Sanjiao toward Jincheng; Chong arrayed camps to pin him, but grain transport did not continue and the three armies starved greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Bo drove from Sanjiao toward Jincheng; Yao Chong drew up camps to contain him, yet supplies failed to arrive and the entire army faced famine.

sentences.zh: 緯言於崇曰：「輔國彌姐高地、建節杜成等皆諸部之豪，位班三品，督運稽留，令三軍乏絕，宜明置刑書，以懲不肅。

translations.literal: Wei said to Chong: "Mijie Gaodi who Supports the State, Du Cheng who Establishes Integrity, and others are magnates of the various tribes, ranked third grade; they supervised transport and delayed, causing the three armies to lack supplies—clear punishment should be applied to warn against lack of discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Wei told Yao Chong: "Mijie Gaodi, the general who supports the state, Du Cheng, who holds the banner of integrity, and others are tribal chiefs of third-rank standing. They were charged with convoys yet stalled them until the army ran dry. Apply the penal code openly to restore discipline.

sentences.zh: 」遂斬之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they executed them.
translations.idiomatic: They executed the negligent officers.

sentences.zh: 諸部大震，租入者五十餘萬。

translations.literal: The tribes were greatly shaken; grain contributions exceeded five hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal levies were terrified into compliance, and more than five hundred thousand measures of grain poured in.

sentences.zh: 興率步騎二萬親討之，勃懼，棄其眾奔于高平公沒奕于，於執而送之。

translations.literal: Xing led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry personally to attack him; Bo feared, abandoned his host and fled to the Duke of Gaoping Moyuyu; Yu seized him and sent him in.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing personally led twenty thousand foot and horse against him; Xue Bo panicked, abandoned his troops, and fled to Moyuyu, Duke of Gaoping, who seized him and handed him over to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 泫氏男姚買得欲因興葬母虵氏殺興，會有告之者，興未之信，遣李嵩詐往。

translations.literal: Yao Maide, Baron of Xuanshi, wished to take advantage of Xing burying mother Lady She to kill Xing; someone informed on him; Xing did not believe it and sent Li Song feigning (a visit).
translations.idiomatic: Yao Maide, a baron of Xuanshi county, plotted to murder Yao Xing during the burial of Lady She. When an informer brought word, Yao Xing doubted the tale and sent Li Song on a pretended errand to probe the matter.

sentences.zh: 買得具以告嵩，嵩還，以聞，興乃賜買得死，誅其黨與。

translations.literal: Maide fully told Song; Song returned and reported; Xing then granted Maide death and executed his associates.
translations.idiomatic: Maide confessed everything to Li Song, who reported back; Yao Xing then forced Maide to take his own life and executed his accomplices.

sentences.zh: 興下書禁百姓造錦繡及淫祀。

translations.literal: Xing issued an edict forbidding the common people from making brocades and excessive sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing promulgated an edict forbidding commoners to weave brocades and to practice illicit, excessive worship.

sentences.zh: 興率眾寇湖城，晉弘農太守陶仲山、華山太守董邁皆降於興。

translations.literal: Xing led the host to raid Hucheng; Tao Zhongshan Administrator of Hongnong for Jin and Dong Mai Administrator of Huashan both surrendered to Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing led his army against Hucheng; Tao Zhongshan, Eastern Jin's Administrator of Hongnong, and Dong Mai, Administrator of Huashan, both capitulated.

sentences.zh: 遂如陝城，進寇上洛，陷之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went to Shancheng, advanced to raid Shangluo, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He then advanced to Shancheng, struck Shangluo, and captured the city.

sentences.zh: 遣姚崇寇洛陽，晉河南太守夏侯宗之固守金墉，崇攻之不克，乃陷柏穀，徙流人西河嚴彥、河東裴岐、韓襲等二萬餘戶而還。

translations.literal: He sent Yao Chong to raid Luoyang; Xiahou Zongzhi Administrator of Henan for Jin firmly held Jinyong; Chong attacked without success, then took Bogu, and relocated the displaced households of Yan Yan from Xihe, Pei Qi and Han Xi from Hedong—more than twenty thousand households—and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yao Chong against Luoyang; Xiahou Zongzhi, Jin's Administrator of Henan, held the Jinyong fortress and repelled him, so Yao Chong turned aside, seized Bogu, and marched away more than twenty thousand displaced households led by Yan Yan of Xihe and Pei Qi and Han Xi of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 興下書，令士卒戰亡者守宰所在埋藏之，求其近親為之立後。

translations.literal: Xing issued an edict ordering that soldiers who died in battle be buried where local officials were; their close kin were sought to establish heirs for them.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing issued an edict requiring local magistrates to bury soldiers fallen in battle within their jurisdictions and to find close kin to continue each man's line.

sentences.zh: 武都氐屠飛、啖鐵等殺隴東太守姚回，略三千餘家，據方山以叛。

translations.literal: The Wu Du Di Tu Fei, Dan Tie, and others killed Yao Hui Administrator of Longdong, plundered more than three thousand households, and held Fangshan in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Fei, Dan Tie, and other Di leaders from Wudu murdered Yao Hui, Administrator of Longdong, ravaged more than three thousand households, and entrenched themselves on Fangshan in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 興遣姚紹等討之，斬飛、鐵。

translations.literal: Xing sent Yao Shao and others to attack them and beheaded Fei and Tie.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing sent Yao Shao and others against them and executed Tu Fei and Dan Tie.

sentences.zh: 遣狄伯支迎流人曹會、牛壽萬餘戶於漢中。

translations.literal: He sent Di Bozhi to welcome the displaced households of Cao Hui and Niu Shou—more than ten thousand households—from Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Di Bozhi to escort more than ten thousand displaced households led by Cao Hui and Niu Shou out of Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 興留心政事，苞容廣納，一言之善，咸見禮異。

translations.literal: Xing attended to government affairs, embraced and tolerated broadly; any good word was treated with special courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing devoted himself to governance, generous in tolerance and eager for counsel; even a single sound suggestion earned distinctive honor.

sentences.zh: 京兆杜瑾、馮翊吉默、始平周寶等上陳時事，皆擢處美官。

translations.literal: Du Jin of Jingzhao, Ji Mo of Fengyi, Zhou Bao of Shiping, and others submitted analyses of current affairs; all were promoted to fine offices.
translations.idiomatic: Du Jin of Jingzhao, Ji Mo of Fengyi, Zhou Bao of Shiping, and others memorialized on policy; each was promoted to a prestigious post.

sentences.zh: 天水姜龕、東平淳于岐、馮翊郭高等皆耆儒碩德，經明行修，各門徒數百，教授長安，諸生自遠而至者萬數千人。

translations.literal: Jiang Kan of Tianshui, Chunyu Qi of Dongping, Guo Gao of Fengyi, and others were aged scholars of great virtue, clear in the classics and cultivated in conduct; each had hundreds of disciples and taught in Chang'an; students coming from afar numbered ten thousand or more.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Kan of Tianshui, Chunyu Qi of Dongping, Guo Gao of Fengyi, and others were eminent elder scholars, masters of the classics and models of conduct; each commanded hundreds of disciples and lectured in Chang'an, while learners arrived from distant regions by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 興每於聽政之暇，引龕等於東堂，講論道藝，錯綜名理。

translations.literal: Xing often in the leisure after hearing cases summoned Kan and others to the eastern hall to lecture on the Way and arts, weaving together names and principles.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever court business allowed, Yao Xing invited Jiang Kan and his peers to the eastern hall to debate learning and sort through philosophical distinctions.

sentences.zh: 涼州胡辯，苻堅之末，東徙洛陽，講授弟子千有餘人，關中後進多赴之請業。

translations.literal: Hu Bian of Liangzhou, at the end of Fu Jian's reign, moved east to Luoyang and taught more than a thousand disciples; many younger scholars from Guanzhong went to seek instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Bian of Liangzhou had relocated east to Luoyang near the end of Fu Jian's rule; he instructed over a thousand pupils, and ambitious young scholars from Guanzhong flocked to study under him.

sentences.zh: 興敕關尉曰：「諸生諮訪道藝，修己厲身，往來出入，勿拘常限。

translations.literal: Xing instructed the gate captain: "Students who inquire into the Way and arts and cultivate themselves—coming and going—do not restrain by usual limits.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing ordered the frontier captains: "Students who pursue learning and cultivate their characters may pass the checkpoints without the usual curfew restrictions.

sentences.zh: 」於是學者咸勸，儒風盛焉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon scholars were all encouraged and Confucian culture flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars took fresh heart, and Confucian learning flourished as never before.

sentences.zh: 給事黃門侍郎古成詵、中書侍郎王尚、尚書郎馬岱等，以文章雅正，參管機密。

translations.literal: Gucheng Shen, Supernumerary Gentleman of the Yellow Gates; Wang Shang, Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat; Ma Dai, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing; and others, by elegant and upright composition, took part in confidential government.
translations.idiomatic: Gucheng Shen, Supernumerary Gentleman of the Yellow Gates; Wang Shang, Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat; Ma Dai, Gentleman at the Masters of Writing; and others—writers of refined, principled prose—were admitted to confidential deliberations.

sentences.zh: 詵風韻秀舉，確然不群，每以天下是非為己任。

translations.literal: Shen's bearing was refined and elevated, assuredly not of the common herd; he always took the rights and wrongs of all under Heaven as his responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Gucheng Shen carried himself with poised distinction; he stood apart from the crowd and habitually treated the moral welfare of the empire as his personal charge.

sentences.zh: 時京兆韋高慕阮籍之為人，居母喪，彈琴飲酒。

translations.literal: At the time Wei Gao of Jingzhao admired Ruan Ji's conduct; during mourning for his mother he played zither and drank wine.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wei Gao of Jingzhao, emulating Ruan Ji, played the zither and drank wine while mourning his mother.

sentences.zh: 詵聞而泣曰：「吾當私刃斬之，以崇風教。

translations.literal: Shen heard and wept, saying: "I ought to cut him down with a private blade to exalt custom and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: When Gucheng Shen heard of it, he wept and swore, "I should run him through with my own sword for the sake of public morality.

sentences.zh: 」遂持劍求高。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he took a sword and sought Gao.
translations.idiomatic: He seized a blade and went looking for Wei Gao.

sentences.zh: 高懼，逃匿，終身不敢見詵。

translations.literal: Gao feared, fled and hid, and to the end of his life dared not meet Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Wei Gao fled into hiding and never again dared face Gucheng Shen.

sentences.zh: 興遣將鎮東楊佛嵩攻陷洛陽。

translations.literal: Xing sent the general Yang Fosong who Stabilizes the East to attack and take Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing dispatched Yang Fosong, General Who Stabilizes the East, who captured Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 班命郡國，百姓因荒自賣為奴婢者，悉免為良人。

translations.literal: He issued orders to the commanderies and kingdoms: among the commoners, those who because of famine had sold themselves to become male or female slaves were all released and made commoners ("good people").
translations.idiomatic: He ordered every commandery and kingdom that all commoners who had sold themselves into slavery because of famine should be freed and restored to free commoner status.

sentences.zh: 興以日月薄蝕，災眚屢見，降號稱王，下書令群公卿士將牧守宰各降一等。

translations.literal: Yao Xing, because the sun and moon were eclipsed and calamities repeatedly appeared, lowered his title and styled himself king; he issued a written order commanding the assembled dukes, ministers, gentlemen, generals, governors, prefects, and magistrates each to descend one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Eclipses of the sun and moon and repeated omens of disaster led Yao Xing to lower his style and call himself king; he issued an edict ordering every noble, minister, official, general, governor, prefect, and county magistrate to step down one rank.

sentences.zh: 於是其太尉趙公旻等五十三人上疏諫曰：「伏惟陛下勳格皇天，功濟四海，威靈振於殊域，聲教暨于遐方，雖成湯之隆殷基，武王之崇周業，未足比喻。

translations.literal: Thereupon his Grand Commandant, Duke Zhao Min, and fifty-two others submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying: "We prostrate ourselves and consider: Your Majesty's merit matches August Heaven, your achievements rescue the four seas, your awesome spirit shakes strange regions, your transforming influence reaches distant quarters—though Cheng Tang's raising the Yin foundation and King Wu's exalting the Zhou enterprise are not enough for comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Duke Zhao Min and fifty-two others jointly memorialized: "We humbly submit: Your Majesty's merit rivals Heaven, your work delivers the four seas, your majesty awakens distant lands, and your civilizing influence reaches the farthest regions; even the grandeur with which Tang founded Yin and King Wu exalted Zhou cannot serve as a fair comparison.

sentences.zh: 方當廓靖江、吳，告成中嶽，豈宜過垂沖損，違皇天之眷命乎！

translations.literal: You are about to sweep clear the Jiang and Wu regions and announce completion at the central marchmount—how should you unduly hang down modest decline and go against August Heaven's caring mandate!"
translations.idiomatic: You are on the verge of pacifying the Jiang and Wu regions and completing your achievement at the sacred central peak—how can you so diminish yourself and turn away from Heaven's favoring mandate!"

sentences.zh: 」興曰：「殷湯、夏禹德冠百王，然猶順守謙沖，未居崇極，況朕寡昧，安可以處之哉！

translations.literal: " Yao Xing said: "Tang of Yin and Yu of Xia in virtue capped the hundred kings, yet still they followed and guarded modest yielding and did not occupy the supreme height; how much more I, ignorant and dim—how can I sit in such a position!"
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing replied: "Tang of Shang and Yu of Xia surpassed all kings in virtue, yet they still held to humility and refused the highest throne. How much less may I, dull and unworthy, presume to occupy it!"

sentences.zh: 」乃遣旻告於社稷宗廟，大赦，改元弘始。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he sent Min to announce it at the altars of soil and grain and the ancestral temple, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Hongshi.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Min report the decision at the altars of soil and grain and the imperial ancestral temple, proclaimed a general amnesty, and adopted the era name Hongshi.

sentences.zh: 賜孤獨鰥寡栗帛有差，年七十已上加衣杖。

translations.literal: He granted millet and silk in graded amounts to the orphaned, solitary, widowed, and childless; to those seventy years of age and older he added clothing and staves.
translations.idiomatic: He distributed grain and silk in set amounts to orphans, the isolated elderly, widows, and widowers; anyone seventy or older also received a robe and a staff.

sentences.zh: 始平太守周班、槐里令李青彡皆以黷貨誅，於是郡國肅然矣。

translations.literal: The prefect of Shiping, Zhou Ban, and the magistrate of Huaili, Li Qingshan, were both executed for corruption; thereupon the commanderies and kingdoms became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhou Ban of Shiping and Magistrate Li Qingshan of Huaili were put to death for taking bribes, after which discipline prevailed across the commanderies and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 洛陽既陷，自淮、漢已北諸城，多請降送任。

translations.literal: After Luoyang had fallen, north of the Huai and Han most of the cities requested to surrender and send hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Once Luoyang had fallen, most of the cities north of the Huai and Han rivers offered submission and sent hostages.

sentences.zh: 興下書聽祖父母昆弟得相容隱。

translations.literal: Yao Xing issued a written order permitting grandparents and siblings of the same parents mutually to conceal one another.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing decreed that grandparents and full siblings might lawfully shield one another from prosecution.

sentences.zh: 姚緒、姚碩德以興降號，固讓王爵，興弗許。

translations.literal: Yao Xu and Yao Shuode, because Yao Xing had lowered his title, firmly declined their princely nobility; Yao Xing would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yao Xing had lowered his own rank, Yao Xu and Yao Shuode repeatedly refused their princely titles; Yao Xing would not allow them to decline.

sentences.zh: 京兆韋華、譙郡夏侯軌、始平龐眺等率襄陽流人一萬叛晉，奔於興。

translations.literal: Wei Hua of Jingzhao, Xiahou Gui of Qiao commandery, Pang Tiao of Shiping, and others led ten thousand refugees from Xiangyang who rebelled against Jin and fled to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hua of Jingzhao, Xiahou Gui from Qiao commandery, Pang Tiao of Shiping, and others led ten thousand displaced people from Xiangyang in revolt against Jin and defected to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 興引見東堂，謂華曰：「晉自南遷，承平已久，今政化風俗何如？

translations.literal: Yao Xing received them in audience in the Eastern Hall and said to Hua: "Since Jin moved south, there has been long peace—how are government, transformation, and customs now?"
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing received them in the Eastern Hall and asked Wei Hua: "Since the Jin court moved south, there has been a long spell of peace—what are governance and popular customs like now?"

sentences.zh: 」華曰：「晉主雖有南面之尊，無總禦之實，宰輔執政，政出多門，權去公家，遂成習俗，刑網峻急，風俗奢宕。

translations.literal: " Hua said: "Though the Jin ruler has the honor of facing south, he has no reality of overall control; the chief ministers hold power, policy issues from many gates, authority has left the ducal house, and it has become custom—the penal net is harsh and urgent, custom is extravagant and dissolute.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hua replied: "The Jin sovereign enjoys nominal supremacy but exercises no unified control; chief ministers hold power, edicts issue from competing factions, and authority has drained from the throne until it is habitual—the laws are harsh and society extravagant and dissolute.

sentences.zh: 自桓溫、謝安已後，未見寬猛之中。

translations.literal: Since Huan Wen and Xie An, one has not seen the mean between lenient and severe."
translations.idiomatic: Since Huan Wen and Xie An, no ruler has struck a sound balance between severity and leniency."

sentences.zh: 」興大悅，拜華中書令。

translations.literal: " Yao Xing was greatly pleased and appointed Hua Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing was delighted and appointed Wei Hua Palace Secretary.

sentences.zh: 興如河東。

translations.literal: Yao Xing went to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing traveled to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 時姚緒鎮河東，興待以家人之禮。

translations.literal: At that time Yao Xu was guarding Hedong; Yao Xing treated him with the courtesy due among family members.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xu was stationed in Hedong; Yao Xing treated him with the intimacy reserved for close kin.

sentences.zh: 下書封其先朝舊臣姚驢磑、趙惡地、王平、馬萬載、黃世等子為五等子男。

translations.literal: He issued a written order enfeoffing the sons of former court ministers of his dynasty—Yao Lü'ai, Zhao Ede, Wang Ping, Ma Wanzai, Huang Shi, and others—as fifth-rank viscounts and barons.
translations.idiomatic: He decreed enfeoffment for the sons of his dynasty's senior ministers—Yao Lü'ai, Zhao Ede, Wang Ping, Ma Wanzai, Huang Shi, and others—as viscounts and barons of the fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 命百僚舉殊才異行之士，刑政有不便於時者，皆除之。

translations.literal: He ordered the hundred officials to recommend men of unusual talent and singular conduct; whatever in punishments and government was not convenient for the times was all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He directed all officials to recommend men of outstanding ability and integrity, and abolished every statute or policy ill suited to the times.

sentences.zh: 兵部郎金城邊熙上陳軍令煩苛，宜遵簡約。

translations.literal: The Gentleman of the Ministry of War, Bian Xi of Jincheng, submitted a statement that military regulations were burdensome and harsh and should follow simplicity and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Xi of Jincheng, an officer in the Ministry of War, argued that military regulations were excessively harsh and should be simplified.

sentences.zh: 興覽而善之，乃依孫吳誓眾之法以損益之。

translations.literal: Yao Xing read it and approved; then he followed the methods of Sun [Wu] and Wu [Qi] for swearing in the host to adjust it by increase or decrease.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing approved the memorial and revised the military code along the lines of the oath-taking assemblies described in the Sunzi and Wuzi traditions.

sentences.zh: 興立律學于長安，召郡縣散吏以授之。

translations.literal: Yao Xing established a school of law in Chang'an and summoned clerks from commanderies and counties to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: He founded a law school in Chang'an and summoned clerks from across the commanderies and counties for instruction.

sentences.zh: 其通明者還之郡縣，論決刑獄。

translations.literal: Those who became thoroughly proficient were sent back to their commanderies and counties to decide criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: Those who mastered the curriculum returned to try criminal cases at their posts.

sentences.zh: 若州郡縣所不能決者，讞之廷尉。

translations.literal: What commanderies, prefectures, or counties could not decide was referred to the Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Cases local authorities could not settle were forwarded to the Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 興常臨諮議堂聽斷疑獄，于時號無冤滯。

translations.literal: Yao Xing often went to the Consultation Hall to hear and decide doubtful cases; at that time he was acclaimed as leaving no wrongful delays.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing regularly heard doubtful lawsuits in the Consultation Hall; people said at the time that innocent verdicts did not languish in the courts.

sentences.zh: 姚緒、姚碩德固讓王爵，許之。

translations.literal: Yao Xu and Yao Shuode firmly declined princely nobility; he permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Xu and Yao Shuode again pressed to surrender their princely titles, Yao Xing granted the request.

sentences.zh: 緒、碩德威權日盛，興恐奸佞小人沮惑之，乃簡清正君子為之輔佐。

translations.literal: Xu and Shuode's awesome authority grew daily; Yao Xing feared that crafty petty men would obstruct and delude them, so he selected upright gentlemen of pure conduct to be their assistants.
translations.idiomatic: As Yao Xu and Yao Shuode's influence grew, Yao Xing worried that sycophants might mislead them, so he appointed principled scholars as their advisers.

sentences.zh: 興以司隸校尉郭撫、扶風太守強超、長安令魚佩、槐里令彭明、倉部郎王年等清勤貞白，下書褒美，增撫邑一百戶，賜超爵關內侯，佩等進位一級。

translations.literal: Because the Metropolitan Governor Guo Fu, the prefect of Fufeng Qiang Chao, the magistrate of Chang'an Yu Pei, the magistrate of Huaili Peng Ming, the Gentleman of the Granaries Wang Nian, and others were pure, diligent, and incorrupt, Yao Xing issued a written order praising them beautifully: he increased Fu's fief by one hundred households, enfeoffed Chao as secondary marquis within the passes, and Pei and the others advanced one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan Governor Guo Fu, Fufeng Prefect Qiang Chao, Chang'an Magistrate Yu Pei, Huaili Magistrate Peng Ming, Granaries Officer Wang Nian, and others were diligent, honest, and upright, so Yao Xing commended them in an edict: Guo Fu's fief gained a hundred households, Qiang Chao received the title of secondary marquis within the passes, and Yu Pei and the rest were promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 使碩德率隴右諸軍伐乞伏乾歸，興潛軍赴之，乾歸敗走，降其部眾三萬六千，收鎧馬六萬匹。

translations.literal: He sent Shuode to lead the armies of Longyou to attack Qifu Gangui; Yao Xing secretly marched an army to join him; Gangui was defeated and fled; he surrendered his followers thirty-six thousand and collected armored horses sixty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yao Shuode to lead the Longyou armies against Qifu Gangui while Yao Xing moved troops secretly to support him. Gangui was routed and fled; Yao Xing accepted the surrender of thirty-six thousand of his followers and seized sixty thousand armored horses.

sentences.zh: 軍無私掠，百姓懷之。

translations.literal: The army did not privately plunder; the hundred surnames cherished it.
translations.idiomatic: The troops took nothing for themselves, and the common people were grateful.

sentences.zh: 興進如枹罕，班賜王公以下，遍于卒伍。

translations.literal: Yao Xing advanced to Fuhan and distributed rewards from dukes and princes downward through the ranks to the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing proceeded to Fuhan and distributed gifts from the nobility down to the common soldiers.

sentences.zh: 興之西也，沒奕於密欲乘虛襲安定，長史皇甫序切諫乃止。

translations.literal: When Yao Xing went west, Moyi Yu secretly wished to exploit the emptiness to raid Anding; Chief Clerk Huangfu Xu remonstrated sharply and only then did he stop.
translations.idiomatic: While Yao Xing marched west, Moyi Yu planned to strike Anding while it was exposed; Chief Clerk Huangfu Xu argued fiercely against it, and he abandoned the idea.

sentences.zh: 于自恨失言，陰欲殺序。

translations.literal: Yu resentfully regretted his loose tongue and secretly wished to kill Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Moyi Yu bitterly regretted having spoken and secretly plotted to murder Huangfu Xu.

sentences.zh: 乞伏乾歸以窮蹙來降，拜鎮遠將軍、河州刺史、歸義侯，復以其部眾配之。

translations.literal: Qifu Gangui, pressed by hardship, came to surrender; he was appointed General Who Extends Afar, Inspector of Hezhou, Marquis Who Returns to Righteousness, and his host was again assigned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui, driven to desperation, submitted; he was named General Who Extends Afar, Inspector of Hezhou, and Marquis Who Returns to Righteousness, and his troops were restored to his command.

sentences.zh: 興下書，將帥遭大喪，非在疆埸險要之所，皆聽奔赴，及期，乃從王役。

translations.literal: Yao Xing issued a written order: generals who suffered a parent's death—if not at a place critical on the border—were all permitted to hurry home for mourning; when the period was complete, they then followed royal service.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing decreed that generals mourning a parent might leave duty for the funeral unless stationed at a vital frontier pass; when mourning ended they were to resume service under the king.

sentences.zh: 臨戎遭喪，聽假百日。

translations.literal: If facing battle when mourning strikes, leave was permitted for one hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Those on campaign when bereavement occurred were granted leave for a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 若身為邊將，家有大變，交代未至，敢輒去者，以擅去官罪罪之。

translations.literal: If one was a border general and a great bereavement struck the family, before a successor arrived, anyone who dared leave without permission was punished by the crime of unauthorized abandonment of office.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier commanders whose families suffered a major loss could not depart until a replacement arrived; anyone who left without authorization was punished as for deserting one's post.

sentences.zh: 遣晉將軍劉嵩等二百三十七人歸於建鄴。

translations.literal: He sent two hundred thirty-seven Jin generals including Liu Song back to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: He repatriated two hundred thirty-seven Jin officers, including Liu Song, to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 魏人襲沒奕于，於棄其部眾，率數千騎與赫連勃勃奔于秦州。

translations.literal: Wei men raided Moyi Yu; Yu abandoned his host and led several thousand horsemen with Helian Bobo to flee to Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei forces attacked Moyi Yu; he deserted his army and fled to Qinzhou with Helian Bobo at the head of several thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 魏軍進次瓦亭，長安大震，諸城閉門固守。

translations.literal: The Wei army advanced and halted at Wating; Chang'an was greatly shaken; the cities closed their gates and firmly guarded.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army advanced to Wating, throwing Chang'an into panic; every city barred its gates and held fast.

sentences.zh: 魏平陽太守貳塵入侵河東。

translations.literal: The prefect of Pingyang in Wei, Erchen, invaded Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Erchen, prefect of Pingyang under Wei, invaded Hedong.

sentences.zh: 興於是練兵講武，大閱於城西，於勇壯異者召入殿中。

translations.literal: Yao Xing thereupon drilled troops and practiced warfare and held a grand review west of the city; among the brave and unusual he summoned them into the palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing then trained his troops, rehearsed tactics, and held a major parade west of the city; men of exceptional valor were summoned into the palace.

sentences.zh: 引見群臣於東堂，大議伐魏。

translations.literal: He received the assembled ministers in audience in the Eastern Hall and debated at length attacking Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the Eastern Hall he received his ministers and held a full debate on attacking Wei.

sentences.zh: 群臣咸諫以為不可，興不從。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers all remonstrated that it could not be done; Yao Xing did not follow them.
translations.idiomatic: Every minister urged against the campaign; Yao Xing would not listen.

sentences.zh: 司隸姚顯進曰：「陛下天下之鎮，不宜親行，可使諸將分討，授以廟勝之策。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Governor Yao Xian advanced and said: "Your Majesty is the pillar of the realm; it is not fitting to go in person—one may send the various generals to attack separately and grant them temple-calculated victorious strategies."
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan Governor Yao Xian said: "Your Majesty anchors the empire; you should not take the field yourself. Send the generals on separate expeditions and supply them with strategies approved at court."

sentences.zh: 」興曰：「王者正以廓土靖亂為務，吾焉得而辭之！」

translations.literal: " Yao Xing said: "The king's proper task is precisely to broaden territory and pacify chaos—how can I decline it!"
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing replied: "A true king exists to expand the realm and put down disorder—how could I shrink from that!"

sentences.zh: 興立其子泓為皇太子，大赦境內，賜男子為父後者爵一級。

translations.literal: Yao Xing established his son Hong as crown prince, proclaimed a general amnesty within the borders, and granted one noble rank to adult males who were heirs for their fathers.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing invested his son Yao Hong as crown prince, proclaimed a general amnesty throughout his realm, and awarded one noble rank to each adult son who was his father's heir.

sentences.zh: 遣姚平、狄伯支等率步騎四萬伐魏，姚碩德、姚穆率步騎六萬伐呂隆。

translations.literal: He sent Yao Ping, Di Bozhi, and others to lead forty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Wei; Yao Shuode and Yao Mu to lead sixty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Lü Long.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Yao Ping and Di Bozhi with forty thousand foot and horse against Wei, and Yao Shuode and Yao Mu with sixty thousand against Lü Long.

sentences.zh: 平等軍次河東，興遣其光遠黨娥、立節雷星、建忠王多等率杏城及嶺北突騎自和寧赴援，越騎校尉唐小方、積弩姚良國率關中勁卒為平後繼，姚緒統河東見兵為前軍節度，姚紹率洛東之兵，姚詳率朔方見騎，並集平望，以會於興。

translations.literal: When Ping and the others' army halted in Hedong, Yao Xing sent his Guangyuan Dang'e, Lijie Leixing, Jianzhong Wang Duo, and others to lead the mounted raiders of Xingcheng and north of the ridges from Hening as reinforcements; Colonel of Rapid Cavalry Tang Xiaofang and Strong Crossbow Yao Liangguo to lead crack troops of Guanzhong as Ping's rear; Yao Xu to command the Hedong troops presently under arms as forward-army coordinator; Yao Shao to lead the troops east of Luo; Shiping Prefect Yao Xiang to lead the Shuofang mounted troops presently under arms—all assembled at Pingwang to join Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Ping's army stopped in Hedong, Yao Xing sent Guangyuan Dang'e, Lijie Leixing, Jianzhong Wang Duo, and others with cavalry from Xingcheng and north of the ridges from Hening as reinforcements; Colonel Tang Xiaofang of the Rapid Cavalry and Strong Crossbow General Yao Liangguo with elite Guanzhong troops as Yao Ping's rear; Yao Xu to coordinate the forward contingent from existing Hedong forces; Yao Shao with troops east of the Luo River; and Shiping prefect Yao Xiang with Shuofang's mounted levies (the sitting prefect, not the late warrior who bore the same name). All were to rally at Pingwang to unite with Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 使沒奕于權鎮上邽，中軍、廣陵公斂權鎮洛陽，姚顯及尚書令姚晃輔其太子泓，入直西宮。

translations.literal: He made Moyi Yu acting governor of Shanggui; Central Army, Duke of Guangling Lian Quan to guard Luoyang; Yao Xian and Palace Secretary Yao Huang to assist the crown prince Hong and attend duty in the Western Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He left Moyi Yu as acting governor of Shanggui, appointed Central Army Commander and Duke of Guangling Lian Quan to hold Luoyang, and assigned Yao Xian and Palace Secretary Yao Huang to assist Crown Prince Yao Hong on duty in the Western Palace.

sentences.zh: 碩德至姑臧，大敗呂隆之眾，俘斬一萬。

translations.literal: Shuode reached Guzang and greatly defeated Lü Long's host, capturing and beheading ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shuode reached Guzang and routed Lü Long's army, killing or capturing ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 隆將呂他等率眾二萬五千，以東苑來降。

translations.literal: Long's general Lü Ta and others led a host of twenty-five thousand and from the Eastern Park came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Long's general Lü Ta and others brought twenty-five thousand men from the Eastern Enclosure to surrender.

sentences.zh: 先是，禿髮利鹿孤據西平，沮渠蒙遜據張掖，李玄盛據敦煌，與呂隆相持。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tufa Ligugu had held Xiping, Juqu Mengxun had held Zhangye, Li Xuansheng had held Dunhuang, and they had faced off with Lü Long.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Tufa Ligugu had occupied Xiping, Juqu Mengxun Zhangye, and Li Xuansheng Dunhuang, while they contended with Lü Long.

sentences.zh: 至是，皆遣使降。

translations.literal: At this point, all sent envoys to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: They now all sent envoys to submit.

sentences.zh: 興率戎卒四萬七千，自長安赴姚平。

translations.literal: Yao Xing led forty-seven thousand soldiers from Chang'an to join Yao Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing marched forty-seven thousand troops from Chang'an to reinforce Yao Ping.

sentences.zh: 平攻魏乾城，陷之，逐據柴壁。

translations.literal: Ping attacked Wei's Qian city, captured it, and then occupied Chaiyu.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Ping took the Wei city of Qian, then advanced to hold Chaiyu.

sentences.zh: 魏軍大至，攻平，截汾水以守之。

translations.literal: The Wei army arrived in great force, attacked Ping, and cut off the Fen River to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: Massive Wei forces besieged Yao Ping and dammed the Fen River to trap him.

sentences.zh: 興至蒲阪，憚而不進。

translations.literal: Yao Xing reached Puban but feared and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing reached Puban but halted out of fear.

sentences.zh: 時碩德攻呂隆，撫納夷夏，分置守宰，節糧積粟，為持久之計。

translations.literal: At that time Shuode was attacking Lü Long, comforting and gathering barbarians and Chinese, dividing and placing guards and magistrates, economizing grain and storing millet, planning for a long endurance.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Yao Shuode was pressing Lü Long, winning over both tribal peoples and Han Chinese, appointing garrison commanders and magistrates, and stockpiling grain for a long campaign.

sentences.zh: 隆懼，遂降。

translations.literal: Long feared and thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Long, terrified, capitulated.

sentences.zh: 碩德軍令齊整，秋毫無犯，祭先賢，禮儒哲，西土悅之。

translations.literal: Shuode's military orders were neat; not a hair's breadth was violated; he sacrificed to former worthies and honored Confucian scholars; the western lands rejoiced in him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shuode's discipline was strict—his men hardly harmed a hair on the people; he sacrificed to past worthies and honored learned men, and the western regions admired him.

sentences.zh: 姚平糧竭矢盡，將麾下三十騎赴汾水而死，狄伯支等十將四萬餘人，皆為魏所擒。

translations.literal: Yao Ping's grain was exhausted and arrows spent; he led thirty riders of his command into the Fen River and died; Di Bozhi and ten other generals and more than forty thousand men were all captured by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Ping ran out of food and arrows, he drowned in the Fen River with thirty horsemen; Di Bozhi and ten other generals with more than forty thousand soldiers were taken captive by Wei.

sentences.zh: 興下書，軍士戰沒者，皆厚加褒贈。

translations.literal: Yao Xing issued a written order: soldiers who died in battle were all generously rewarded and ennobled posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing decreed generous posthumous honors for every soldier killed in action.

sentences.zh: 魏軍乘勝進攻蒲阪，姚緒固守不戰，魏乃引還。

translations.literal: The Wei army exploited victory to advance and attack Puban; Yao Xu firmly guarded and did not fight; Wei thereupon led away and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army pressed on to Puban, but Yao Xu held the defenses and refused battle, so Wei withdrew.

sentences.zh: 興徙河西豪右萬餘戶于長安。

translations.literal: Yao Xing moved more than ten thousand households of powerful families from west of the river to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing resettled over ten thousand wealthy households from west of the Yellow River in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 晉輔國將軍袁虔之、甯朔將軍劉壽、冠軍將軍高長慶、龍驤將軍郭恭等貳于桓玄，懼而奔興。

translations.literal: Jin's Assistant General Who Supports the State Yuan Qianzhi, General Who Calms the North Liu Shou, General Who Champions Gao Changqing, General Who Inspires Awe Guo Gong, and others turned against Huan Xuan in fear and fled to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Jin generals Yuan Qianzhi, Liu Shou, Gao Changqing, Guo Gong, and others who had sided against Huan Xuan fled in alarm to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 興臨東堂引見，謂虔之等曰：「桓玄雖名晉臣，其實晉賊，其才度定何如父也？

translations.literal: Yao Xing went to the Eastern Hall and received them in audience, saying to Qianzhi and the others: "Though Huan Xuan bears the name of a Jin minister, in truth he is a Jin traitor—how do his talent and measure compare with his father's?
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing received them in the Eastern Hall and asked Yuan Qianzhi and the rest: "Huan Xuan may call himself a Jin minister, but he is really a traitor—how do his abilities compare with his father's?

sentences.zh: 能辦成大事以不？

translations.literal: Can he accomplish a great enterprise or not?
translations.idiomatic: Can he accomplish a great undertaking or not?"

sentences.zh: 」虔之曰：「玄籍世資，雄據荊、楚，屬晉朝失政，遂偷竊宰衡。

translations.literal: " Qianzhi said: "Xuan relies on inherited position, dominates Jing and Chu; due to the Jin court losing government, he stole the chief minister's power.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qianzhi replied: "Huan Xuan rests on his family's prestige and controls Jingzhou and Chu; with the Jin court in disorder he has usurped the chief minister's authority.

sentences.zh: 安忍無親，多忌好殺，位不才授，爵以愛加，無公平之度，不如其父遠矣。

translations.literal: Cruel and tolerant of no kin, many suspicions and fond of killing, ranks not matched to talent, noble titles added by favor—he has no measure of fairness; he is far inferior to his father.
translations.idiomatic: He is ruthless toward his own kin, suspicious and murderous, hands out offices and titles by whim rather than merit—nothing like fair rule—and falls far short of his father.

sentences.zh: 今既握朝權，必行篡奪，既非命世之才，正可為他人驅除耳。

translations.literal: Now that he already holds court power, he is sure to carry out usurpation; since he is not a talent who commands the age, he can only clear the way for others.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he controls the court he will surely seize the throne; lacking the stature to rule an era, he will only pave the way for someone else.

sentences.zh: 此天以機便授之陛下，願速加經略，廓清吳、楚。

translations.literal: This is Heaven using a convenient moment to grant Your Majesty—wish speedily to apply strategy and sweep clear Wu and Chu."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is handing Your Majesty the opening—move quickly to plan the conquest and pacify Wu and Chu."

sentences.zh: 」興大悅，以虔之為大司農，餘皆有拜授。

translations.literal: " Yao Xing was greatly pleased and appointed Qianzhi Grand Minister of Agriculture; the rest all received appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing was delighted, named Yuan Qianzhi Grand Minister of Agriculture, and gave the others posts as well.

sentences.zh: 虔之固讓，請疆埸自效，改授假節、甯南將軍、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Qianzhi firmly declined and requested to show effort on the border; he was changed and appointed credential-bearing General Who Calms the South, Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qianzhi insisted on declining and asked to serve on the frontier; he was instead given the credential-bearing title of General Who Calms the South and Inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 興立其昭儀張氏為皇后，封子懿、弼、洸、宣、諶、愔、璞、質、逵、裕、國兒皆為公。

translations.literal: Yao Xing established his honored consort of the Zhaoyi rank, Lady Zhang, as empress and enfeoffed his sons Yi, Bi, Guang, Xuan, Chen, Yin, Pu, Zhi, Kui, Yu, Guo'er all as dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing elevated his Zhaoyi consort, Lady Zhang, to empress and enfeoffed his sons Yao Yi, Yao Bi, Yao Guang, Yao Xuan, Yao Chen, Yao Yin, Yao Pu, Yao Zhi, Yao Kui, Yao Yu, and Yao Guo'er as dukes.

sentences.zh: 遣其兼大鴻臚梁斐，以新平張構為副，拜禿髮傉檀車騎將軍、廣武公，沮渠蒙遜鎮西將軍、沙州刺史、西海侯，李玄盛安西將軍、高昌侯。

translations.literal: He sent his concurrent Grand Herald Liang Fei, with Deputy Zhang Gou of Shiping, to invest Tufa Nutan as General of Chariots and Cavalry and Duke of Guangwu, Juqu Mengxun as General Who Guards the West, Inspector of Shazhou, Marquis of Xihai, and Li Xuansheng as General Who Pacifies the West, Marquis of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Concurrent Grand Herald Liang Fei with Shiping's Zhang Gou as deputy to invest Tufa Nutan as General of Chariots and Cavalry and Duke of Guangwu, Juqu Mengxun as General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Shazhou with the marquisate of Xihai, and Li Xuansheng as General Who Pacifies the West and Marquis of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 興遣鎮遠趙曜率眾二萬西屯金城，建節王松忿率騎助呂隆等守姑臧。

translations.literal: Yao Xing sent General Who Extends Afar Zhao Yao to lead twenty thousand hosts to camp west at Jincheng; Wang Songfen of Jianjie to lead cavalry to assist Lü Long and the others in guarding Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent General Who Extends Afar Zhao Yao with twenty thousand men to encamp west of Jincheng and Jianjie officer Wang Songfen with cavalry to help Lü Long hold Guzang.

sentences.zh: 松忿至魏安，為傉檀弟文真所圍，眾潰，執松忿，送于傉檀。

translations.literal: Songfen reached Wei'an and was surrounded by Nutan's younger brother Wenzhen; the host collapsed; Songfen was seized and sent to Nutan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Songfen reached Wei'an, where Tufa Nutan's brother Wenzhen surrounded him; his force broke and Wenzhen captured him and sent him to Nutan.

sentences.zh: 傉檀大怒，送松忿還長安，歸罪文真，深自陳謝。

translations.literal: Nutan was greatly angry and sent Songfen back to Chang'an, returning blame to Wenzhen and deeply apologizing himself.
translations.idiomatic: Nutan was furious but sent Wang Songfen back to Chang'an, blamed Wenzhen, and offered a contrite apology.

sentences.zh: 興下書，錄馬嵬戰時將吏，盡擢敘之，其堡戶給復二十年。

translations.literal: Yao Xing issued a written order recording officers and clerks from the battle at Mawei and promoting them all; the fortress households were granted exemption from labor for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing ordered a roster of everyone who had served at the Battle of Mawei and promoted them all; households in those fortresses received twenty years of tax and labor exemption.

sentences.zh: 興性儉約，車馬無金玉之飾，自下化之，莫不敦尚清素。

translations.literal: Yao Xing's nature was frugal and restrained; carriages and horses had no gold or jade ornament; from below they were transformed by him—none failed to esteem purity and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing lived simply—his carriages bore no gold or jade—and his example spread downward until everyone favored austerity.

sentences.zh: 然好游田，頗損農要。

translations.literal: Yet he loved roaming and hunting and somewhat harmed agricultural essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he loved the chase, which somewhat harmed farming.

sentences.zh: 京兆杜挻以僕射齊難無匡輔之益，著《豐草詩》以箴之，馮翊相雲作《德獵賦》以諷焉。

translations.literal: Du Ting of Jingzhao, because Vice Director Qi Nan had no benefit of aiding and supporting, composed "The Luxuriant Grass Poem" to admonish him; Xiang Yun of Fengyi composed "The Virtuous Hunt Rhapsody" to indirectly criticize.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ting of Jingzhao wrote "The Luxuriant Grass" to reproach Vice Director Qi Nan for failing to counsel the throne; Xiang Yun of Fengyi composed "The Virtuous Hunt" as a hunting satire.

sentences.zh: 興皆覽而善之，賜以金帛，然終弗能改。

translations.literal: Yao Xing read both and approved them, granting them gold and silk, yet in the end could not change.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing read both pieces with approval and rewarded the authors with gold and silk, yet he never reformed his habits.

sentences.zh: 晉順陽太守彭泉以郡降興，興遣楊佛嵩率騎五千，與其荊州刺史趙曜迎之，遂寇陷南鄉，擒建威將軍劉嵩，略地至於梁國而歸。

translations.literal: Jin's prefect of Shunyang, Peng Quan, surrendered his commandery to Yao Xing; Yao Xing sent Yang Fosong to lead five thousand cavalry with his Inspector of Jingzhou Zhao Yao to welcome him; they then raided and captured Nanxiang, seized General Who Establishes Might Liu Song, plundered territory reaching Liang state and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Quan, Jin prefect of Shunyang, yielded his commandery; Yao Xing sent Yang Fosong with five thousand horsemen and his Inspector of Jingzhou, Zhao Yao, to receive him. They then stormed Nanxiang, captured General Who Establishes Might Liu Song, raided as far as Liang commandery, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 又遣其兼散騎常侍席確詣涼州，征呂隆弟超入侍，隆遣之。

translations.literal: He also sent his concurrent Palace Attendant Xi Que to Liangzhou to summon Lü Long's younger brother Chao to attend court as hostage; Long sent him.
translations.idiomatic: He also dispatched Concurrent Palace Attendant Xi Que to Liangzhou to demand that Lü Long send his brother Lü Chao to the capital as a hostage; Lü Long complied.

sentences.zh: 呂隆懼禿髮傉檀之逼，表請內徙。

translations.literal: Lü Long feared Tufa Nutan's pressure and memorialized requesting removal inland.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful of Tufa Nutan, Lü Long petitioned to be resettled inland.

sentences.zh: 興遣齊難及鎮西姚詰、鎮遠乞伏乾歸、鎮遠趙曜等步騎四萬，迎隆於河西。

translations.literal: Yao Xing sent Qi Nan and General Who Guards the West Yao Jie, General Who Extends Afar Qifu Gangui, General Who Extends Afar Zhao Yao, and others with forty thousand infantry and cavalry to welcome Long west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing sent Qi Nan with General Who Guards the West Yao Jie, General Who Extends Afar Qifu Gangui, General Who Extends Afar Zhao Yao, and forty thousand foot and horse to escort Lü Long from west of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 難至姑臧，以其司馬王尚行涼州刺史，配兵三千鎮姑臧，以將軍閻松為倉松太守，郭將為番禾太守，分戍二城，徙隆及其宗室僚屬于長安。

translations.literal: When Nan reached Guzang, he had his Chief Clerk Wang Shang act as Inspector of Liangzhou, assigned three thousand troops to guard Guzang, made General Yan Song prefect of Cangsong and Guo Jiang prefect of Fanhe, dividing garrisons in two cities; he moved Long and his clan and officials to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Nan reached Guzang, he put his chief clerk Wang Shang in charge as Inspector of Liangzhou with three thousand men to hold the city, appointed General Yan Song prefect of Cangsong and Guo Jiang prefect of Fanhe to garrison those two towns, and relocated Lü Long with his kinsmen and staff to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜遣弟如子貢其方物。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun sent his younger brother to present local produce as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun sent his younger brother with tribute of regional goods.

sentences.zh: 王尚綏撫遺黎，導以信義，百姓懷其惠化，翕然歸之。

translations.literal: Wang Shang comforted and gathered the surviving people, guiding them with trust and righteousness; the hundred surnames cherished his kindly transformation and uniformly returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shang soothed the survivors, ruling through good faith, and the people welcomed his kindness and rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 北部鮮卑並遣使貢款。

translations.literal: The northern tribes of Xianbei all sent envoys to offer submission and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Xianbei tribes all sent envoys with tribute and pledges of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 桓玄遣使來聘，請辛恭靖、何澹之。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan sent an envoy to court and requested Xin Gongjing and He Danzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan dispatched a diplomatic mission asking for Xin Gongjing and He Danzhi.

sentences.zh: 興留恭靖而遣澹之，謂曰：「桓玄不推計曆運，將圖篡逆，天未忘晉，必將有義舉，以吾觀之，終當傾覆。

translations.literal: Yao Xing retained Gongjing but sent Danzhi, saying to him: "Huan Xuan does not defer to the counted fortune of the mandate and intends to plot usurpation; Heaven has not forgotten Jin—there is sure to be a righteous rising; as I see it, he will in the end overturn;
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing kept Xin Gongjing but released He Danzhi, telling him: "Huan Xuan ignores the turning of Heaven's mandate and plots usurpation. Heaven has not abandoned Jin—a righteous movement will arise. In my view he is doomed to fall;

sentences.zh: 卿今馳往，必逢其敗，相見之期，遲不雲遠。

translations.literal: If you gallop there now, you are sure to meet his defeat; the time we meet again is not far off in the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Ride south now and you will arrive in time for his ruin; we shall meet again before long."

sentences.zh: 」初，恭靖至長安，引見興而不拜，興曰：「朕將任卿以東南之事。

translations.literal: " Earlier, when Gongjing reached Chang'an, he was led to audience with Yao Xing but did not bow; Yao Xing said: "I intend to entrust you with affairs of the southeast."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Xin Gongjing had reached Chang'an, Yao Xing summoned him but he refused to bow. Yao Xing said, "I mean to put you in charge of affairs in the southeast."

sentences.zh: 」靖曰：「我寧為國家鬼，不為羌賊臣。

translations.literal: " Jing said: "I would rather be a ghost for the state than be minister to Qiang bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Xin Gongjing replied, "I would sooner be a loyal ghost of Jin than a minister to Qiang brigands."

sentences.zh: 」興怒，幽之別室。

translations.literal: " Yao Xing was angry and imprisoned him in a separate chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing, enraged, had him confined in a separate cell.

sentences.zh: 至是，恭靖亦逾牆遁歸。

translations.literal: At this point, Gongjing also climbed the wall and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: By then Xin Gongjing had also scaled a wall and escaped homeward.

sentences.zh: 興遣其將姚碩德、姚斂成、姚壽都等率眾三萬，伐楊盛于仇池。

translations.literal: Xing dispatched his generals Yao Shuode, Yao Liancheng, Yao Shoudu, and others to lead a host of thirty thousand and attack Yang Sheng at Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing sent Generals Yao Shuode, Yao Liancheng, and Yao Shoudu at the head of thirty thousand men to campaign against Yang Sheng in Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 壽都等入自宕昌，斂成從下辯而進。

translations.literal: Shoudu and others entered from Dangchang; Liancheng advanced from Xiabian.
translations.idiomatic: Shoudu’s column came in through Dangchang; Liancheng drove up from Xiabian.

sentences.zh: 盛遣其弟壽距成，從子斌距都。

translations.literal: Sheng sent his younger brother Shou to oppose Cheng, and his nephew Bin to oppose Du.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sheng sent his brother Yang Shou to hold Liancheng at bay and his nephew Yang Bin to face Shoudu.

sentences.zh: 都逆擊擒之，盡俘其眾。

translations.literal: Du counterstruck, captured them, and took all their host prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Shoudu counterattacked, took them captive, and rounded up their entire force.

sentences.zh: 楊壽等懼，率眾請降。

translations.literal: Yang Shou and the others feared; they led the host and asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shou and his men, stricken with fear, brought their troops forward and offered submission.

sentences.zh: 碩德還師。

translations.literal: Shuode returned the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shuode withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 晉汝南太守趙策委守奔於興。

translations.literal: Jin’s Administrator of Runan, Zhao Ce, abandoned the defense and fled to Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ce, Jin’s prefect of Runan, threw over his post and defected to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 興如趙逍園，引諸沙門于澄玄堂聽鳩摩羅什演說佛經。

translations.literal: Xing went to the Zhao Xiao Garden and led various śramaṇas to the Chengxuan Hall to listen to Kumārajīva expound Buddhist scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing visited the Zhao Xiao Garden and gathered śramaṇas in the Chengxuan Hall to hear Kumārajīva lecture on the sutras.

sentences.zh: 羅什通辯夏言，尋覽舊經，多有乘謬，不與胡本相應。

translations.literal: Kumārajīva was thoroughly eloquent in Chinese speech; when he examined old scriptures, many erred and missed the mark and did not correspond to the Hu originals.
translations.idiomatic: Kumārajīva commanded Chinese with fluency and precision; when he reviewed older translations, he found them often wrong and out of step with the Indic originals.

sentences.zh: 興與羅什及沙門僧略、僧遷、道樹、僧睿、道坦、僧肇、曇順等八百餘人，更出大品，羅什持胡本，興執舊經，以相考校，其新文異舊者皆會於理義。

translations.literal: Xing with Kumārajīva and śramaṇas Seng Lüe, Seng Qian, Dao Shu, Seng Rui, Dao Tan, Seng Zhao, Tan Shun, and more than eight hundred others again produced the Great Perfection; Kumārajīva held the Hu original, Xing held the old scripture, and they examined one another; where the new text differed from the old, all accorded with principle and meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing joined Kumārajīva and more than eight hundred monks—among them Seng Lüe, Seng Qian, Dao Shu, Seng Rui, Dao Tan, Seng Zhao, and Tan Shun—in issuing a fresh translation of the Great Perfection of Wisdom Sutra: Kumārajīva read from the Indic manuscript while Yao Xing followed the old Chinese text, line by line, so that wherever the new wording departed from the former, it aligned with sound doctrine.

sentences.zh: 續出諸經並諸論三百餘卷。

translations.literal: They continued to produce various sutras together with various treatises, more than three hundred fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: They went on to issue over three hundred fascicles of additional sutras and śāstras.

sentences.zh: 今之新經皆羅什所譯。

translations.literal: The new scriptures of today are all translated by Kumārajīva.
translations.idiomatic: The “new” scriptures in circulation today are Kumārajīva’s work.

sentences.zh: 興既托意於佛道，公卿已下莫不欽附，沙門自遠而至者五千餘人。

translations.literal: Since Xing entrusted his intentions to the Buddha-Way, none from the dukes and ministers downward failed to revere and attach themselves; śramaṇas who came from afar were more than five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yao Xing committed himself to the Dharma, every minister and noble under him rushed to follow suit, and more than five thousand monks converged from distant regions.

sentences.zh: 起浮圖於永貴裏，立波若台于中宮，沙門坐禪者恆有千數。

translations.literal: He raised a stūpa in Yonggui Ward, established a Prajñā terrace in the inner palace, and seated-meditation śramaṇas were constantly numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He built a stūpa in Yonggui Ward and a Prajñā terrace inside the palace; monks meditating in hall numbered in the thousands day after day.

sentences.zh: 州郡化之，事佛者十室而九矣。

translations.literal: Prefectures and commanderies were transformed by it; of those who served the Buddha, nine houses in ten.
translations.idiomatic: The practice spread through every prefecture and commandery until nine households in ten took up devotion to the Buddha.

sentences.zh: 使姚碩德及冠軍徐洛生等伐仇池，又遣建武趙琨自宕昌而進，遣其將斂俱寇漢中。

translations.literal: He sent Yao Shuode and Champion General Xu Luosheng and others to attack Chouchi; he also dispatched Establishes Martial Might Zhao Kun to advance from Dangchang, and sent his general Lian Ju to raid Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yao Shuode and Champion General Xu Luosheng to strike Chouchi, sent General Who Establishes Martial Might Zhao Kun in from Dangchang, and tasked his officer Lian Ju with raiding Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 時劉裕誅桓玄，迎復安帝，玄衛將軍、新安王桓謙，臨原王桓怡，雍州刺史桓蔚，左衛將軍桓謐，中書令桓胤，將軍何澹之等奔於興。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Yu executed Huan Xuan and welcomed and restored Emperor An; Huan Xuan’s Guard General and Prince of Xin’an Huan Qian, Prince of Linyuan Huan Yi, Inspector of Yongzhou Huan Wei, Guard General of the Left Huan Mi, Palace Secretary Huan Yin, General He Danzhi, and others fled to Xing.
translations.idiomatic: While Liu Yu put Huan Xuan to death and restored Emperor An to the throne, Huan Qian—Huan Xuan’s Guard General and Prince of Xin’an—along with Prince of Linyuan Huan Yi, Yongzhou inspector Huan Wei, Left Guard General Huan Mi, Palace Secretary Huan Yin, General He Danzhi, and others took refuge with Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 劉裕遣大參軍衡凱之詣姚顯，請通和，顯遣吉默報之，自是聘使不絕。

translations.literal: Liu Yu sent Senior Army Advisor Heng Kaizhi to visit Yao Xian to request opening peace; Xian sent Ji Mo to reply; from this envoys on missions did not cease.
